title: The Sweet Tide
premise: Lior Kavanagh, a wedding planner who stopped believing in weddings after her own collapsed fifteen years ago, has built a careful life of small safe steps on a coastal island town. When Noor Adeyemi — the stranger behind ten years of anonymous letters that once kept Lior from giving up entirely — moves in next door, the two are pulled into planning the season's last great wedding: the inheritance-contingent marriage of Lior's estranged brother. As duty, family secrets, and a decade of unspoken feeling collide, Lior must finally say the sentence she has rehearsed for ten years before the last ferry of the season departs — and Noor must decide whether staying is braver than leaving.
about_author: Ada Villalobos is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent a decade writing other people's vows before writing her own stories. She lives near the water and believes every love story deserves at least one impossible deadline.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry Schedule
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. We meet her mid-wedding, flawless on the surface, hollow underneath; she recites the ferry timetable like a prayer. A letter arrives — the tenth anniversary of an anonymous correspondence that once saved her. Emotional beat: guarded longing disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Number Fourteen
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor moves into the cottage next door with boxes of unsent replies and a job offer she hasn't accepted. She recognizes Lior instantly but says nothing. Beat: quiet dread and hope tangled together.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Neighbors meet over a broken fence and borrowed sugar; Lior feels inexplicably seen. Her brother Declan calls: he's engaged, and their grandmother's will requires the wedding happen on the island by season's end or the house goes to developers. Beat: duty crashing into sanctuary.

chapters.title: The Contract
chapters.summary: Declan's POV. Declan, pragmatic and wounded, explains the inheritance trap to his fiancée Priya, who agrees for reasons of her own. He hires Lior to plan it, knowing she'll refuse nothing that keeps the family house standing. Beat: resentment wearing a business suit.

chapters.title: Letters I Never Sent
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Flashback chapter: how Noor began writing to a stranger whose story she overheard in a hospital waiting room ten years ago, and why she stopped. Beat: guilt over a kindness that became a lie of omission.

chapters.title: Tide Charts and Guest Lists
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior and Noor are thrown together when Noor volunteers to help with the wedding. Their chemistry is immediate and inconvenient. Lior notices Noor flinches at the word 'letters.' Beat: attraction sharpened by suspicion.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Knew
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya discovers the will's fine print: the marriage must be genuine, witnessed by the grandmother's old lawyer, who knew more about the family than anyone admits. Beat: the stakes turn personal and legal at once.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The lawyer hints that Declan's engagement may not survive scrutiny, and that Lior herself was named in an earlier draft of the will. Meanwhile a storm cancels vendors, forcing Lior and Noor into a long night of improvisation. Beat: intimacy under pressure.

chapters.title: The Almost
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. During the storm blackout, Noor nearly confesses everything; instead she kisses Lior, then pulls away, terrified the truth will poison it. Beat: desire outrunning honesty, then paying for it.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years Ago
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Flashback: the wedding that never happened, the fiancé who left, the year Lior stopped believing in ceremonies. We learn the letters arrived exactly when she needed them most. Beat: grief reframed as origin story.

chapters.title: Priya's Doubt
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya realizes Declan loves the house more than her — and that she may love someone else entirely. She asks Lior, off the record, whether a wedding can be honest if its reasons aren't. Beat: complicity between two women trapped in other people's plans.

chapters.title: The Handwriting
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior finds a draft letter in Noor's recycling bin — in the handwriting of her decade-long correspondent. She says nothing, but begins testing Noor with details only the letter-writer could know. Beat: betrayal and hope in the same breath.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinner
chapters.summary: Declan's POV. The rehearsal dinner detonates: the lawyer questions the couple publicly, Declan accuses Lior of sabotage, and Priya goes silent. Noor defends Lior fiercely — too fiercely. Beat: family fracture in candlelight.

chapters.title: Confessions at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Cornered by Lior on the beach, Noor admits she wrote the letters — all of them — and that she moved here deliberately, hoping to be forgiven or hated, either one better than silence. Beat: raw exposure; Lior walks away.

chapters.title: The Empty Week
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior throws herself into the wedding logistics while refusing to speak to Noor. But rereading the letters, she realizes every word of comfort was real even if the anonymity wasn't. Beat: anger curdling into understanding.

chapters.title: What Priya Decided
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya tells Declan the truth: she won't marry him, inheritance or not. The house now hangs on nothing. Declan, stripped of his plan, finally grieves their mother properly for the first time. Beat: liberation through refusal.

chapters.title: The Lawyer's File
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The lawyer reveals the earlier will left the house to Lior — contingent only on her being happy, as judged by a letter he was asked to write. The grandmother had read the anonymous letters too. Beat: the past rewriting itself kindly.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Heartbroken and certain she's ruined everything, Noor books passage on the final ferry. At the dock she finds Lior waiting with every letter bundled in twine. Beat: the deadline made flesh.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Both POVs interwoven. On the dock, as the ferry horn sounds, Lior finally says the sentence rehearsed for ten years: 'It was you who taught me to stay, so stay.' Noor misses the boat on purpose. Beat: catharsis; the arc's emotional summit.

chapters.title: A Wedding After All
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Declan, freed, helps Lior stage the island's first wedding she actually believes in — small, honest, unplanned: theirs, witnessed by Priya and the lawyer. The house is saved not by contract but by testimony. Beat: joy earned through wreckage.

chapters.title: High Water Mark
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Settling into number fourteen for good, Noor writes one last letter and hand-delivers it next door. Lior reads it aloud on the porch. Beat: tenderness without fear for the first time.

chapters.title: The Sweet Tide
chapters.summary: Shared epilogue POV. One year later: the ferry schedule changes, the business thrives, and Lior plans weddings again — but only ones where everyone tells the truth first. Final image: two names carved side by side on the fence they rebuilt. Beat: peace, chosen daily.
